svg.title: How a lead flows through LeadFlow AI
svg.desc: Animated diagram. Example leads move from the web form through schema check, screening, the duplicate check, the existing-account check, and the rep filter. New prospects go to the buyer agent and capacity service in parallel, then the routing agent, validation and commit, and the rep handoff. Other leads stop at dropped, self_serve, duplicate, preserve_owner, ownership_exception, or no_eligible_reps.
svg.text: Submits the form: Intercom contract ends in 2 weeks, needs 40 seats before Q1
Schema valid: required fields, work email, phone, company size
Passes screening: not a test, competitor, or non-ICP submission
No existing account for finpay.es, so this is a new prospect
5 eligible reps in EMEA-Southern: Mid-Market, Spanish, active, under cap, in hours
The shortlist goes to both agents at once
In parallel: the buyer agent reads intent (workbook expects 95, High) and the capacity service scores the 5 reps
The routing agent proposes a primary and a backup rep from the 5
Both reps are checked against the shortlist, then the assignment is committed
The rep gets the buyer brief, and the decision is saved
An automated staging test submits the form
Screening finds a test or bot address
Dropped before any agent or rep sees it
Asks about a chat widget for a college side project
Screening: company size 1-15 is below the sales-assisted segment
No earlier submission from this email
harborpay.com is an existing customer owned by Mark Rivera (rep_002)
Owner kept and a handoff brief generated, with no agent calls
Asks about an enterprise compliance plan
No earlier submission from this email
atlasgroup.com has two accounts with different owners: rep_009 and rep_038
Sent to RevOps as an ownership exception, listing both owners
